title.en: How to Form the Croatian Future Tense
title.hr: Kako se tvori buduće vrijeme u hrvatskom

grammar.intro:
The Croatian future tense (**futur I**) is formed with a **short form of htjeti** (to want / will) + the **infinitive** of the main verb.

The short forms are: **ću, ćeš, će, ćemo, ćete, će** — these are clitics and cannot stand first in a sentence.

The **negative** future uses: **neću, nećeš, neće, nećemo, nećete, neće** — these are full (non-clitic) forms and CAN stand first.

rules.label: Positive future: ću/ćeš/će + infinitive
rules.explanation:
Attach the correct short form of **htjeti** to the subject, then follow with the **infinitive** of the main verb:

- **Ja ću ići.** – I will go.
- **Ti ćeš raditi.** – You will work.
- **On/Ona će doći.** – He/She will come.
- **Mi ćemo pričati.** – We will talk.
- **Vi ćete vidjeti.** – You (pl.) will see.
- **Oni/One će kupiti.** – They will buy.

The infinitive always ends in **-ti** (or **-ći** for verbs like ići).

examples.en: Tomorrow I will go to the sea.
We will eat at a restaurant.

rules.label: Negative future: neću/nećeš/neće + infinitive
rules.explanation:
Replace the short form with the **negative form** — these are stressed and can appear at the start of a sentence:

- **neću** – I will not
- **nećeš** – you will not
- **neće** – he/she/it will not
- **nećemo** – we will not
- **nećete** – you (pl.) will not
- **neće** – they will not

The infinitive follows directly after the negative form.

examples.en: I will not go to the party.

rules.label: Word order: clitic position and time adverbs
rules.explanation:
Because **ću/ćeš/će...** are clitics, they sit in **second position** — after the first word or phrase:

- *Sutra **ću** ići.* (Tomorrow I will go.) — 'Sutra' is first, clitic follows.
- *Ana **će** doći.* (Ana will come.) — subject is first, clitic follows.

The **long/emphatic** forms **hoću/hoćeš/hoće...** can be used for emphasis or in short answers, but are less common in everyday speech.

Yes/no questions use **Hoćeš li...?** or **Ćeš li...?** + infinitive.

rules.label: Time expressions for the future
rules.explanation:
Common time expressions used with the future tense:

- **sutra** – tomorrow
- **prekosutra** – the day after tomorrow
- **večeras** – this evening / tonight
- **uskoro** – soon
- **sljedeći tjedan** – next week
- **sljedeće godine** – next year
- **za tjedan dana** – in a week's time
- **za sat vremena** – in an hour

examples.hr: Za tjedan dana bit ćemo u Dubrovniku.
examples.en: In a week's time we will be in Dubrovnik.
Tonight we will watch a film.

paragraphs.hr: Ana će ostati još tri dana u Hrvatskoj. Marko joj je predložio da zajedno posjete Dubrovnik. Ana je odmah pristala jer oduvijek želi vidjeti stari grad.
paragraphs.en: Ana will stay three more days in Croatia. Marko suggested they visit Dubrovnik together. Ana agreed immediately because she has always wanted to see the old city.

paragraphs.hr: Sutra ujutro će krenuti autobusom. Vožnja će trajati oko četiri sata. Marko je rekao da će put biti lijep jer prolaze pokraj mora.
paragraphs.en: Tomorrow morning they will set off by bus. The journey will take about four hours. Marko said the trip will be lovely because they pass along the sea.

paragraphs.hr: U Dubrovniku će hodati po gradskim zidinama. Pogled s zidina na more i stare kuće bit će nevjerojatan. Ana planira napraviti mnogo fotografija.
paragraphs.en: In Dubrovnik they will walk along the city walls. The view from the walls over the sea and old houses will be incredible. Ana plans to take many photos.

paragraphs.hr: Za ručak će probati lokalne specijalitete s mora. Marko zna jedan dobar restoran gdje ćete jesti svježe ribe i školjke po povoljnoj cijeni.
paragraphs.en: For lunch they will try local seafood specialities. Marko knows a good restaurant where you can eat fresh fish and shellfish at a good price.

paragraphs.hr: Poslijepodne će uzeti brod do otoka Lokruma. Na Lokrumu će se kupati i odmoriti u sjeni. Brod se vraća navečer.
paragraphs.en: In the afternoon they will take a boat to Lokrum island. On Lokrum they will swim and rest in the shade. The boat returns in the evening.

paragraphs.hr: Ana je rekla da će se sigurno vratiti sljedećeg ljeta. Hrvatska joj se jako svidjela i želi pokazati grad svojoj obitelji. Marko je rekao da će je čekati.
paragraphs.en: Ana said she will definitely come back next summer. She liked Croatia very much and wants to show the city to her family. Marko said he will wait for her.

readingQuestions.prompt: How will Ana and Marko travel to Dubrovnik?
readingQuestions.promptHr: Kako će Ana i Marko putovati do Dubrovnika?
readingQuestions.explanation: 'Sutra ujutro će krenuti autobusom.' — They will travel by bus.

readingQuestions.prompt: What will they do on the city walls?
readingQuestions.promptHr: Što će raditi na gradskim zidinama?
readingQuestions.explanation: 'Hodat će po gradskim zidinama' and 'Ana planira napraviti mnogo fotografija.' — They will walk and Ana will take photos.

readingQuestions.prompt: What will they eat for lunch in Dubrovnik?
readingQuestions.promptHr: Što će jesti za ručak u Dubrovniku?
readingQuestions.explanation: 'ćete jesti svježe ribe i školjke' — they will eat fresh fish and shellfish.

readingQuestions.prompt: Where will they go in the afternoon?
readingQuestions.explanation: 'Poslijepodne će uzeti brod do otoka Lokruma.' — In the afternoon they will take a boat to Lokrum island.

readingQuestions.prompt: When does Ana say she will return to Croatia?
readingQuestions.promptHr: Kada Ana kaže da će se vratiti u Hrvatsku?
readingQuestions.explanation: 'Ana je rekla da će se sigurno vratiti sljedećeg ljeta.' — Ana said she will come back next summer.

test.prompt: Which is the correct future form for 'I will go'?
test.explanation: First person singular: 'ću'. 'Ja ću ići.'

test.prompt: Which is the correct future form for 'She will work'?
test.explanation: Third person singular: 'će'. 'Ona će raditi.'

test.prompt: Which is the correct future form for 'We will eat'?
test.explanation: First person plural: 'ćemo'. 'Mi ćemo jesti.'

test.prompt: Which is the correct future form for 'You (plural) will see'?
test.explanation: Second person plural: 'ćete'. 'Vi ćete vidjeti.'

test.prompt: Which is the correct future form for 'They will come'?
test.explanation: Third person plural: 'će'. 'Oni će doći.'

test.prompt: Which sentence correctly says 'I will not go to school'?
options: Ja ću ne ići u školu.
test.explanation: Negative future: 'neću' + infinitive. 'Neću ići u školu.'

test.prompt: Which sentence correctly says 'He will not eat meat'?
test.explanation: 'Neće' is the third person singular negative future: 'On neće jesti meso.'

test.prompt: Which sentence correctly says 'We will not travel by bus'?
test.explanation: 'Nećemo' is first person plural negative future: 'Mi nećemo putovati autobusom.'

test.prompt: Translate: 'Tomorrow I will call you.'
test.explanation: 'Sutra ću te nazvati.' — first person singular future 'ću' + infinitive 'nazvati'.

test.prompt: Translate: 'She will not forget the meeting.'
test.explanation: 'Neće' = she will not. 'Ona neće zaboraviti sastanak.'

test.prompt: What does 'prekosutra' mean?
test.explanation: 'Prekosutra' = the day after tomorrow.

test.prompt: What does 'za tjedan dana' mean?
test.explanation: 'Za tjedan dana' = in a week's time.

test.prompt: What does 'uskoro' mean?
test.explanation: 'Uskoro' = soon.

test.prompt: How do you ask 'Will you come tomorrow?' in Croatian?
test.explanation: Yes/no questions in the future use 'Hoćeš li...?': 'Hoćeš li doći sutra?'

test.prompt: How do you say 'Shall we go together?' as a suggestion?
test.explanation: 'Hoćemo li...?' is the first person plural question for suggestions: 'Hoćemo li ići zajedno?'

test.prompt: Choose the correct word order: 'Tomorrow we will travel to Zagreb.'
options: Mi ćemo sutra putovati u Zagreb.
Both A and B are correct.
test.explanation: Both 'Mi ćemo sutra putovati' and 'Sutra ćemo putovati' are grammatically correct — the clitic comes after the first phrase either way.

test.prompt: Which is the correct negative future for 'you (singular) will not study'?
test.explanation: Second person singular negative future: 'nećeš'. 'Nećeš učiti.'

test.prompt: What does 'Večeras ćemo gledati film.' mean?
options: Last night we watched a film.
Tonight we will watch a film.
We always watch films in the evening.
We are watching a film now.
test.explanation: 'Večeras' = tonight/this evening; 'ćemo gledati' = we will watch.

test.prompt: Which sentence means 'You (plural) will not forget this'?
test.explanation: 'Nećete' = you (plural) will not. 'Nećete zaboraviti ovo.'

test.prompt: What is the emphatic/long form of 'ću' (I will)?
test.explanation: The long form of the first person singular future auxiliary is 'hoću'.

test.prompt: Translate: 'Next year they will visit Croatia.'
test.explanation: 'Sljedeće godine će posjetiti Hrvatsku.' — Note: 'posjetit će' is an alternative contracted spelling also correct in Croatian.

test.prompt: Which time expression means 'this evening / tonight'?
test.explanation: 'Večeras' = this evening / tonight. 'Jutros' = this morning; 'sinoć' = last night.

test.prompt: Choose the correct future sentence: 'I will drink coffee tomorrow morning.'
test.explanation: 'Sutra ujutro ću piti kavu.' — correct future: 'ću' + infinitive 'piti'.

test.prompt: How do you say 'Will you (singular) eat dinner with us?'
options: Jesi li jeo večeru s nama?
Hoćeš li jesti večeru s nama?
Jesi li jesti večeru s nama?
test.explanation: 'Hoćeš li jesti...?' is the correct yes/no question in the future for second person singular.

test.prompt: Which sentence correctly says 'In an hour we will be at the airport.'?
options: Za sat vremena bit ćemo na aerodromu.
Za sat vremena smo bili na aerodromu.
Za sat vremena ćemo na aerodromu.
Za sat vremena bili ćemo na aerodromu.
test.explanation: 'Bit ćemo' is the future of biti (to be) — 'biti' + 'ćemo'. 'Za sat vremena bit ćemo na aerodromu.'

items.hr: Hoćemo li se naći u sedam?

items.en: Shall we walk around the city?
